annotation.title_clean: Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 on the safety of toys and repealing Directive 2009/48/EC
annotation.title_en: Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 on the safety of toys and repealing Directive 2009/48/EC
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: EU Regulation replacing the Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with directly applicable rules on toy safety, covering chemicals, economic operator duties, conformity assessment, CE marking and a digital product passport. It states that toys with AI or digital elements must also comply with the AI Act and Cyber Resilience Act, and it requires mental-health risk assessment for connected toys.
key_provisions_or_claims: Toys must meet general and particular essential safety requirements, with due regard to the precautionary principle.
Generic bans on CMR substances, endocrine disruptors, PFAS and 34 bisphenols in toys.
Mandatory digital product passport and CE marking, with customs verification at the border.
Connected toys must comply with the AI Act, the Cyber Resilience Act and the Radio Equipment Directive; safety assessments must consider risks to mental health.
Online marketplaces must treat non-compliant toy offers as illegal content under the DSA.
